articles.title: Too nice: do Arsenal lack the grit and tenacity to end WSL title drought?
articles.summary: Renée Slegers’ team have the technical ability, but doubts remain over the nastiness needed to rival Manchester City and Chelsea. Arsenal, 10 points adrift of the Women’s Super League leaders, are poised to undertake a “big review” of their season during this international break to try to determine…
body: The technical ability throughout the world-class squad Arsenal have assembled could hardly be higher but the levels of grit, resilience and tenacity need examining in a group that appear unable to match Chelsea and Manchester City when it comes to the mental aspects of a title race. Arsenal last won the WSL in 2019.

When speaking to sources close to the Arsenal players, it is common to hear of the squad being like a “family”, very supportive of each other and full of “great people”. Those admirable traits, and a general sense the club is full of nice characters, often come across when watching games or during player interviews. Arsenal have built a team of good eggs; polite, courteous and professional individuals who people would be glad to call friends. In the vast majority of scenarios in life this is, quite obviously, a good thing. But are they too nice to beat City?

articles.title: South Africa in running to stage Africa’s first Olympics as 2036 race hots up
articles.summary: Qatar frontrunners of bidders, with India and Hungary. Turkey, Germany and Korea to present to IOC next month. South Africa is in the hunt to stage Africa’s first Olympics after it was named as one of seven countries that will formally present its case to host the 2036 Games in November.
body: However its bid, which would probably be spread across Cape Town, Johannesburg and Durban, is seen as a distinct outsider, with Qatar widely regarded as the frontrunner ahead of India and Hungary.

Turkey, Germany and South Korea make up the remaining countries that have been asked to present to the International Olympic Committee’s future bid committee next month, marking the first stage of a process that will end with a vote in 2029.

Qatar’s position at the top of the pecking order is partly down to the perceived strength of the bid and the fact that Asia will not have hosted a Games since Tokyo 2020. However a Doha Olympics would have to be moved from the Games’ traditional July-August slot due to the heat.
India is seen as the closest challenger, although its bid to host in Ahmedabad is seen to have slipped back during the past 18 months.

articles.title: USA will be 'underdogs' in 2027 Ryder Cup - Furyk
articles.summary: United States Ryder Cup captain Jim Furyk says his team will be "underdogs" when they attempt to end more than 30 years of pain on European soil in next year's edition at Adare Manor.
body: United States captain Jim Furyk says his team will be "underdogs" when they attempt to end more than 30 years of pain on European soil in next year's Ryder Cup at Adare Manor.
The Americans have not claimed an away Ryder Cup victory since 1993, losing all seven contests in Europe since that victory at The Belfry.

Furyk, who oversaw a 17½-10½ loss to Europe in France in 2018, was handed a second stint as captain earlier this year following Keegan Bradley's team's defeat to Luke Donald's Europe at Bethpage Black in 2025.

"We know what we are up against, we also know it's been 34 years since we won in Europe. There is no secret, I'm going to hear it over and over again so I am going to embrace it," Furyk said during a news conference at Adare Manor in County Limerick.

articles.title: F1 drivers face ‘unhealthy’ Singapore air as ‘super’ El Niño fuels wildfire haze
articles.summary: F1 circus greeted by smoky skies before this Sunday’s GP. Pollution affects reaction times like ‘alcoholic beverage’ Singapore’s Formula One night race is an annual opportunity for the city-state to showcase its dazzling, illuminated skyline.
body: The south-east Asian nation is shrouded in a thick haze that has drifted from huge wildfires in neighbouring Indonesia, with Singapore now among the world’s most polluted cities.
Haze is a recurring problem in Singapore during Indonesia’s dry season, but conditions have worsened this year as a “super” El Niño exacerbates fires across parts of Sumatra and Kalimantan.

“Rainfall across the region has been about 80% below normal since June, fuelling the most intense fire season in over a decade,” said Wang Jingyu, an assistant professor at Singapore’s National Institute of Education at Nanyang Technological University.

Air quality levels in Singapore were classified as “unhealthy” on Tuesday by the country’s National Environment Agency and F1’s travelling circus will be greeted by smoky skies when it arrives from Kuala Lumpur following Sunday’s eventful race at Sepang.

articles.title: Djokovic ends title drought with China Open triumph while Alcaraz claims glory in Japan
articles.summary: Serb victorious after De Minaur retires injured. Alcaraz beats Lehecka for first title since February. Novak Djokovic capped an outstanding week at the China Open with his first title for nearly a year.
body: The 7-6, 0-1 victory means Djokovic has won at least one title in each of the past 21 years, while he now has 102 tour level trophies overall. Both men reached the final without having to complete their matches on Monday – Djokovic thanks to the much-publicised disqualification of Daniil Medvedev, while De Minaur’s opponent Hubert Hurkacz pulled the plug because of injury.

Djokovic edged a very tight first set on a tie-break before the two men each took a medical timeout, but it came as a big surprise when De Minaur abruptly shook hands after winning the opening game of the second set. The Australian, who returned to court with strapping on his left thigh, said in his on-court interview: “I want to say sorry to all the amazing fans that came to watch this match. I didn’t want to finish like this.”

When Djokovic lost in the opening round of the US Open amid ongoing physical struggles, the sporting obituaries were being prepared, but the Serb has shown once again that writing him off would be premature.

articles.title: UEFA monitoring Man City case before deciding on potential action
articles.summary: UEFA is monitoring Manchester City’s financial case and will wait for the Premier League disciplinary process to conclude before considering whether to take any action of its own.
body: An independent commission found City guilty of serious financial-rule breaches covering nine seasons between 2009/10 and 2017/18, with five of the upheld charges relating to compliance with UEFA’s Financial Fair Play regulations.
Sky Sports reports European football’s governing body is following developments but does not intend to make a decision while City’s challenge against the findings remains unresolved.
City lodged their appeal last Thursday and continue to deny wrongdoing, arguing that the commission’s conclusions contain significant errors of law, principle and fact.
The commission found that City’s owners used what it described as “sham” commercial arrangements to disguise funding as sponsorship revenue over several years.

articles.title: Was it right to default Medvedev for hitting spectator with ball?
articles.summary: Daniil Medvedev was defaulted for hitting a spectator with the ball during his semi-final with Novak Djokovic at the China Open, but was it the correct decision or should he have been able to continue playing?
body: Medvedev was trailing Djokovic 7-5 5-3 and had lost a point when he hit the ball coming off the wall.
The spectator, who was ​sitting in the first row behind Medvedev, clutched his left eye and appeared to ‌be in pain as he walked out of the gallery, assisted by stadium staff.

Speaking to Sky Sports, Jonathan Overend said: "From the first camera angle we saw the ball leaving Medvedev's racket and weren't sure where it had gone, but I later saw a different angle filmed from the stands and it clearly went straight from the racket into the face of this spectator and so from the minute that was obvious, it was an instant default.

"It was absolutely the correct decision. The rulebook is very clear about that and it was unfortunate for Medvedev. We take him at face value when he says he didn't mean to do it, but it did leave his racket with force and it did strike the spectator.

articles.title: The Jets should change their running back approach
articles.summary: Over the last couple of years, one thing that has frustrated me with the Jets’ approach to offense has been their insistence on using Breece Hall as a do it all back. Hall is a very talented player, but I think it’s clear that he isn’t a complete back.
body: With Hall out of the lineup in Week 4 against the Chicago Bears, Braelon Allen took over the lead running back role.

There wasn’t much that went right for the Jets offensively in that game, but Allen played some solid football. While there were no highlight reel runs, Allen ended the day with a very respectable 59 yards on 14 carries.

In many ways that has been the story of Braelon Allen’s young career. The 2024 fourth round pick out of Wisconsin has a career average per rushing attempt of 3.7 yards, which is underwhelming. Allen’s career long run is only 20 yards. But he pairs it with an above average success rate of 51.7% on runs.
Against the Bears, Allen was steady if unspectacular. He posted a robust 57% success rate despite not breaking a run longer than 10 yards.
points: Over the last couple of years, one thing that has frustrated me with the Jets’ approach to offense has been their insistence on using Breece Hall as a do it all back.
Hall is a very talented player, but I think it’s clear that he isn’t a complete back.

articles.title: UEFA monitoring Man City case as it considers potential action
articles.summary: UEFA is monitoring developments and will wait until the end of the Premier League's disciplinary process before deciding whether to take any potential action against Manchester City.
body: City have been found guilty by an independent commission of breaking the Premier League's financial rules between 2009 and 2018, including five charges of failing to comply with UEFA's Financial Fair Play rules.
UEFA financial rules at the time meant clubs were effectively limited to spending what they earned within set break-even requirements.
The independent commission found that City's owners put in £830m of their own money and disguised it as sponsorship income for nine seasons.
City are appealing against the decision and maintain they have a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence which will clear their name.
